q: Which law is most directly associated with strong internal controls, accurate financial reporting, and reporting control weaknesses?
why: SOX focuses on corporate governance, financial reporting, and internal controls.

q: A US bank is investigating an unauthorized electronic transfer. Which rule is the strongest match?
why: Regulation E governs consumer protection for electronic transfers and unauthorized transactions.

q: Which US law is linked most clearly to whistleblower protections in the study guide?
why: The guide associates the Dodd-Frank Act with whistleblower protection.

q: Which legal instrument targets insider trading and market manipulation?
why: The Market Abuse Regulation promotes transparent, fair markets and prevents insider trading and market manipulation.

q: Secure Customer Authentication and open banking are core features of which EU instrument?
why: PSD2 covers secure electronic payments, SCA, open banking, licensing, and transparency.

q: False representation, failure to disclose, and abuse of position are the three principal offences under which law?
why: These are the three fraud offences highlighted under the UK Fraud Act.

q: Which UK law creates the failure-to-prevent-fraud offence for organizations?
why: ECCTA creates corporate liability where an employee or agent commits fraud benefiting the organization and reasonable procedures are absent.

q: Which UK framework is associated with a 50/50 PSP split, an £85,000 cap, and reimbursement within five business days in most cases?
why: The guide links those APP-reimbursement figures to the regime based on FSMA.

q: Which law regulates the collection, access, and distribution of consumer credit-reporting data in the US?
why: FCRA governs consumer credit-reporting information and related rights and responsibilities.

q: Which law is mentioned when assessing grounds for asset recovery or freezing before closing a fraud investigation?
why: The guide refers to the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 in the case-closure and evidence context.

q: Which jurisdiction uses the CA$5,000 threshold distinction in the study guide?
why: Canada: above CA$5,000 carries a maximum 14 years; below CA$5,000 carries a maximum 2 years.

q: Which item below is a regulatory or enforcement body rather than a law?
why: OLAF is the European Anti-Fraud Office; it is not a legal instrument.
